audits.mathematicalReason: Let r be the radius and x=OE. Because E lies inside the circle, EA=r+x and EB=r−x. Intersecting chords give r²−x²=DE·EF=12. Right triangle DOE gives r²+x²=DE²=36. Adding yields r²=24, so the area is 24π. The alternative route is also valid: join CF. Since CD is a diameter, angle DFC is right, and triangles DOE and DFC are similar. Their corresponding sides give r/8=6/(2r), again yielding r²=24. Thus both optional geometric routes support the assessed circle-area calculation without requiring their union.

figureEvidence.fact: The order along the horizontal diameter is A–O–E–B, and the order along the chord is D–E–F; hence E is internal to both chords.
The perpendicular diameters meet at O, so triangle DOE is right at O; C, D, and F lie on the circle.

audits.derivedAnswer: D: AB=9 and CD=4, giving an area of 78 square units.
audits.mathematicalReason: Write AB=a, CD=c, and BC=w, with B=(0,0), C=(w,0), A=(0,a), and D=(w,c). The midpoint O of diameter AD has height (a+c)/2. Tangency makes this height the radius, so AD=a+c. Pythagoras therefore gives w²+(a−c)²=(a+c)², or w=2√(ac). The trapezoid area is (a+c)√(ac). The five choices give 4√3, 7√10, 10√21, 78, and 16√55, respectively. Only 78 is an integer. Midsegment geometry can establish the midpoint projections used here. Alternatively, if T is the tangency point, BT=TC=w/2 and angle ATD is right; similar right triangles ABT and TCD give ac=BT·TC. Both listed routes are defensible.

figureEvidence.fact: A and D lie on the same side of BC, with AB and CD perpendicular to BC; these are the parallel bases of trapezoid ABCD.
AD passes through center O, and the circle is tangent to segment BC, so the perpendicular distance from O to BC is its radius.

audits.mathematicalReason: A single perforated 3×3×3 block contains 20 unit cubes: eight corner cubes and twelve edge-center cubes. There are 24 face-sharing pairs, since each corner cube meets three edge-center cubes. Counting cube-face incidences gives its surface area as 6·20−2·24=72. The twenty large blocks also have 24 shared interfaces in the first-stage arrangement. After the second removal, each interface retains eight unit-square contacts, because its central unit square is removed on both sides. Consequently the final surface area is 20·72−2·24·8=1056. Decomposition into cube constituents and surface-area calculations fit the assessed scopes. The identity 6N=S+2I explicitly accounts for the double multiplicity of internal shared faces.

figureEvidence.fact: The illustrated first-stage solid retains corner and edge-center blocks, with openings at the face centers leading into the central tunnel system.

The retained blocks are aligned face-to-face on a cubic grid. Shared faces are internal rather than exposed surface; the second-stage removal is specified by the stem, not depicted as already completed.

audits.mathematicalReason: The small, nonoverlapping cuts leave one surviving middle portion of each of the prism's 12 original edges. Each of the eight corner cuts creates a triangular face with three new edges, none shared with another cut face. Thus the total is 12+8·3=36. This directly uses addition and multiplication in disjoint edge classes, supported by the original prism's structure.

figureEvidence.fact: The illustrated corner slices join points strictly inside the three edges incident to a corner, producing triangular cut faces while leaving middle portions of the original edges.

audits.mathematicalReason: Drop perpendiculars AH and BK to DC. Rectangle ABKH gives AH=BK and HK=4. The right triangles ADH and BCK are congruent by HL, so DH=KC=(10−4)/2=3 and DK=7. Let N be the midpoint of DF. Since B is the midpoint of DE, the midsegment BN is parallel to EF and therefore perpendicular to DF. Thus N=K, giving DF=2DK=14 and CF=14−10=4. For the coordinate route, set D=(0,0), C=(10,0), A=(x,h), and B=(x+4,h). Pythagoras on the equal legs gives x²+h²=(6−x)²+h², which reduces to the linear equation 12x=36. Hence B=(7,h), E=(14,2h), and F=(14,0). Both routes support the segment and midpoint calculations.

AB is parallel to DC, and the marked right angle is at F, so EF is perpendicular to the common line DF and DC.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the floor have n tiles along each side. Each diagonal contains n tiles. If n is even, the diagonal tile sets are disjoint and contain 2n black tiles, an even number. Thus 101 black tiles forces n to be odd. For odd n the two sets share exactly the central tile, so their union contains 2n−1 tiles. Solving 2n−1=101 gives n=51, and the total is 51²=2601. The finite-union formula is explicitly within cnm_h009, and parity is appropriate support.

figureEvidence.fact: The corner patches show black tiles following both diagonals; the central patch illustrates their shared central tile in an odd-sided grid.
The drawing is a partial grid illustration, so its displayed patches are not used to infer the actual number of rows or columns.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let G be the intersection of the medians. The centroid ratios give BG=(2/3)·8=16/3 and CG=(2/3)·12=8. Their perpendicularity yields [BGC]=(1/2)(16/3)(8)=64/3. Also, [BGC]:[DGC]=BG:GD=2:1 because these triangles have a common altitude to BD. Since D is the midpoint of AC, [BDC]=[ABC]/2. Combining these relations gives [ABC]=3[BGC]=64. This uses the correctly oriented centroid division and justified median area relations, with the triangle-area formula as support.

figureEvidence.fact: BD and CE intersect at the labeled point G, and the right-angle marker at G indicates their perpendicularity.
D lies on AC and E lies on AB. Their midpoint status follows from the stated median conditions, not from measuring the sketch.

audits.mathematicalReason: A grid 20 cells high and 10 cells wide has 21 horizontal grid lines, each containing 10 toothpicks, and 11 vertical grid lines, each containing 20 toothpicks. These orientation classes are disjoint, so the total is 21·10+11·20=210+220=430. Counting by lines counts every shared cell boundary only once and directly matches combined addition and multiplication counting.

figureEvidence.fact: The brackets label the grid as 20 toothpick lengths high and 10 toothpick lengths wide, with both exterior boundaries included.
Adjacent square cells share a single toothpick along their common side; the gaps in the drawing indicate continuation of the rectangular grid.
